With the able assistance of Ms. Kaushik, learned amicus curiae, the matter has been settled.
2. The petitioner shall deposit Rs. 18 lakhs on or before 20.11.2023 in the name of the Registrar General of Delhi High Court which shall be put in an interest-bearing fixed deposit.

3. The petitioner shall give proof of the deposit both to the respondent as well as the learned amicus curiae and within 7 days thereafter, the respondent will cooperate in filing for the second motion.

After recording of the second motion, the respondent shall cooperate in quashing of the FIR No.
784/2018 registered under Section 316/377/323/498A/504/506/34 IPC at PS Hardoi City, U.P.
4.
On the date the FIR is quashed, the Registry will prepare a DD in the name of the respondent along with up-to-date accrued interest and the This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/11/2023 at 21:46:19 same shall be handed over to the respondent.
5. All the litigation costs shall be borne by the petitioner.
6. With these directions and binding the parties to their obligations stated above, the present contempt petition is disposed of.
